text.p: The following are some of the leading stories in Finnish papers this morning.
HELSINGIN SANOMAT
- Coffee price to rise a couple of markka per half kg this spring after global wholesale prices have risen over 50 percent, Finnish roasters say.

- Pohjola CEO Iiro Viinanen improves his offer to mutual Suomi's policy holders, promising better returns than for new clients in Pohjola's planned life-insurer Henki-Pohjola, due to take over Suomi's insurance portfolio. @
- UPM-Kymmene's plans to pay 3.00 markka of its 4.50 markka dividend in Rauma shares is questionable, says Jarmo Leppiniemi, chairman of the Finnish private shareholder lobby.
- Finns have been divided in three categories -- the eurosuccesses, the ordinary people and the underclass -- researcher says.
- Finnish ministers have been actively paying off their debts since joining cabinet and Prime Minister Paavo Lipponen and Finance Minister Sauli Niinisto are debt-free, report to parliament shows. @
- Age becomes an obstacle to getting jobs already at 35, researcher says.
- Partek planning to build houses for about 400 residents next to its headquarters in Sornainen in Helsinki.
- Eastern Europe's transitional economies cannot be analysed with current economics, says professor Douglas North, winner of the 1993 Nobel economics prize, visiting Helsinki.

- Public companies may lie about their plans under certain circumstances, but the bigger a planned project, the better founded it is to require answers from management, says justice ministry chief of staff Kirsti Rissanen. @
- Managing director and owner of textile designer Marimekko Kirsti Paakkanen plans to list her company in Helsinki, says needs funds for "development project abroad".
KAUPPALEHTI
- Life insurance market will grow to 20 billion markka this decade from 12 billion markka last year, says Sampo CEO Jouko Leskinen.
- Oil and energy group Neste setting up five separate business operations in China which all have potential to become the group's main business, Neste official says. @
- Suddenly liquid Finnish stock market hungry for share issues, but analysts do not expect more supply than last year's 4.8 billion markka.
AAMULEHTI

- Defence minister Anneli Taina surpised at poll showing 83 percent of Finns believe the country's leaders are secretly preparing NATO membership, says there are no such plans and such an issue would certainly be openly debated.
- Pressure from the Central Organisation of Finnish Trade Unions (SAK) has compelled Postipankki to start planning deposit accounts with no charges for withdrawals. @
HUFVUDSTADSBLADET
- Insurer A-Vakuutus launches special car insurance policy for women, some 15 percent cheaper than for men since their accident risk is lower.
- Animals transported in Finland treated well, says animal rights organisation Animalia.
-- Helsinki Newsroom +358-9-680 50 242
